class.name: SerializerOptions
class.brief_description: Typed options of the text formats of [ResourceTextSerializer].

members.member: CSV: the delimiter between cells, one character, for example [code]";"[/code] for spreadsheets in many European languages or [code]"\t"[/code] for tab-separated values. Used for writing and reading. Other values (empty, longer than one character, a quote or a line break) fall back to [code]","[/code].

CSV: if [code]true[/code], the first row holds the property names and only the columns that are used are written; reading maps the cells by these names. If [code]false[/code], there is no header row: every stored property of the element class is written as a column, in property order, and reading maps the cells by position. Use the same value for writing and reading.

JSON, INI, XML and TOML: values of the root resource that are equal to the same property of [member defaults] are not written (metadata is always written). Nested resources are written completely. Used by the settings servers to write only changed settings. Reading is not affected: missing keys keep the defaults of the class.
All formats: if [code]true[/code], enum properties are written as their names ([code]"High"[/code]); if [code]false[/code], as numbers ([code]2[/code]). Both are read.

All formats: vectors, rectangles, transforms and colors hold 32-bit floats. If [code]false[/code], each is written as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same 32-bit value ([code]0.1[/code]). If [code]true[/code], the exact value is written ([code]0.10000000149011612[/code]), for tools that compare the text with 64-bit values. [float] properties are 64-bit and always written exactly. Has no effect in builds with [code]precision=double[/code] for vectors.

JSON, INI, XML and TOML: if [code]true[/code], the class of the root resource is written ([code]"$type"[/code], the XML attribute [code]type[/code]). If [code]false[/code], it is left out, for example for data sent to a server that knows the type; such text must be read with a type hint (the [code]type_hint[/code] argument of [method ResourceTextSerializer.deserialize]), and [ResourceLoader] does not recognize it as a resource file. Nested resources whose class differs from the declared type always keep their type.
JSON and XML: the indentation of one level. An empty string writes JSON on one line and XML without line breaks. INI, CSV and TOML ignore it.

INI: if [code]true[/code], values are written without type syntax ([code]name=Ann[/code], [code]size=1, 2[/code]), so players and other tools can edit them. If [code]false[/code], values use the Variant syntax of [ConfigFile] ([code]name="Ann"[/code], [code]size=Vector2(1, 2)[/code]). Both are read.

JSON, INI, XML and TOML: if [code]true[/code], the keys of every object, section and element are written in alphabetical order (also the keys of [Dictionary] properties), which keeps diffs in version control small. If [code]false[/code], properties are written in property order. CSV columns always keep the property order.
XML: if [code]true[/code], the text starts with [code]<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>[/code]. Both are read.
